draft.title: Neurotypical and neurodivergent
card: Neurotypical
describes a person whose brain develops and works in ways that most people's do. Their thinking, learning and behaviour fit what is usual in the population.
Neurodivergent
describes a person whose brain works in ways that differ from what is usual. Autism and ADHD are examples. Being neurodivergent is a difference, not a sign of illness.
Adaptive
an emotion, behaviour or thought that helps a person cope, function and reach their goals in daily life.
Maladaptive
an emotion, behaviour or thought that gets in the way of coping or functioning for that person. It depends on its effect on the person, not on whether it is common.
draft.remember: Neurotypical and neurodivergent describe how a brain works compared with most. Adaptive or maladaptive describes how it affects the person.

a.q: Which statement best describes a neurodivergent person?
opts: Their brain works in ways that differ from what is usual
Their brain has an illness that must be treated
Their thoughts and behaviours are maladaptive
Their brain works in the same way as most people's
a.why: Neurodivergent describes a brain that works differently from what is usual. It does not mean illness or maladaptive behaviour, because it describes a difference and not how well the person functions.
a.clue: It describes a difference from what is usual, not a fault.

b.q: Priya is neurotypical. Before exams she avoids all study and stays awake all night worrying, and this stops her from sitting the papers. How should her behaviour be described?
opts: Maladaptive, because it stops her from functioning
Adaptive, because most students feel nervous
Adaptive, because she is neurotypical
Maladaptive, because she is neurotypical
b.why: Her behaviour is maladaptive because it stops her from coping with a task she needs to do. Being neurotypical says how her brain compares with most, not whether her behaviour helps her, so it cannot make the behaviour adaptive.
b.clue: Ask what the behaviour does to her ability to function.

a.best: Their brain works in ways that differ from what is usual

b.best: Maladaptive, because it stops her from functioning

problems.detail: In 'Adaptive or maladaptive describes how it affects the person', 'it' grammatically refers back to how a brain works. The card applies adaptive and maladaptive to an emotion, behaviour or thought, not to the brain. A student could read this as saying neurodivergence itself is adaptive or maladaptive.
The clue 'It describes a difference from what is usual' almost repeats the right option's wording ('differ from what is usual'), so a student can match words without understanding the idea.
